[BugFix]: isolate draft attention config from target (#22752)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
In vLLM 0.33.0, attn_vllm_config can return the target model’s
VllmConfig directly. When draft attention initializes, assigning the
draft’s parallel_config to that shared object can overwrite the target’s
pipeline and expert parallel settings. This patch makes a shallow copy
first. Only the copy’s parallel_config is reassigned, so the draft also
retains any attention settings supplied by upstream.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
It fixes a stall on the first prefill request observed with EAGLE3, four
pipeline stages, and expert parallelism enabled.

### How was this patch tested?
A separate Ascend A3 run tested the same fix on commit 71ffe0c92 with
vLLM 0.33.0. With the fix, the same request returned HTTP 200 in 14.60
seconds.

[Performance][MoE] Eliminate All2AllV dispatch split host sync (#21907)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`TokenDispatcherWithAll2AllV._preprocess` currently blocks the host
twice per
MoE dispatch:

- `torch.repeat_interleave(...,
num_global_tokens_per_local_expert.ravel())`
infers its output length from device values, causing an implicit D2H
copy and
  stream synchronization.
- The single-local-expert path calls `torch.npu.synchronize()`.

This PR keeps the split accounting on device and defers host access:

- Reuses pinned CPU staging buffers for the two split D2H copies.
- Guards both copies with one NPU event instead of synchronizing in
  `_preprocess`.
- Enqueues `npu_moe_token_permute` before waiting on that event.
- Copies the split values after the event so returned numpy metadata
does not
  alias the reusable staging buffers.
- Passes an explicit `output_size` to `repeat_interleave`.
- Removes the full-device synchronization from the single-local-expert
path.

No environment variable, public API, or user configuration is added. The
`MoEAllToAllCombineMetadata` contract is unchanged.

This implementation also addresses the pinned-staging race discussed in
#17670.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. All2AllV MoE dispatch no longer performs synchronous split D2H
copies or
the single-local-expert full-device synchronization. A3 measurements
show a
7.9% reduction in host dispatch time and a 0.63% reduction in 8K-prefill
TTFT.
A release note fragment is included.

### How was this patch tested?

## Tested revisions

| Revision | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `4b3bd7ebe51094f3afa5288bb7a3316d12d3154e` | Current upstream/main
base |
| `93c9ecd76aa0ef59e2c44f5d6c995fb96af97eb6` | Dispatcher implementation
and unit tests |
| `40e81bd97` | Added the release note |
| `c4aea965b` | Final PR head, isolating split staging in the CPU unit
test |
| vLLM `4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5` | A3 runtime revision
|

## A3 validation environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | A3, 2 x Ascend910, 64 GiB HBM per device |
| CANN | 9.1.0 |
| Python | 3.11.10 |
| torch / torch-npu | 2.10.0+cpu / 2.10.0.post7 |
| EvalScope | 1.14.1 |
| Model | `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w4a8` |
| Serving | TP2 + EP, eager, 8192 max batched tokens |

## Unit tests

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_token_dispatcher.py
```

Result: `31 passed, 11 skipped`.

CPU UT CI matrix at `c4aea965b`:

The added cases cover permute-before-event ordering, non-blocking split
copies,
independent numpy ownership, zero received tokens, one local expert, one
EP
rank, and explicit `repeat_interleave(output_size=...)`.

## A3 kernel benchmark

The kernel sequence used the production model shape: 8192 tokens, top-k
10,
512 experts, EP2, hidden size 2560. Baseline and candidate outputs
matched for
splits, permutation mapping, permuted tokens, and repeated expert IDs.
Five
warm-up iterations were followed by 50 measured iterations.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Host dispatch mean | 0.4015 ms | 0.3697 ms | -7.9% |
| Host dispatch p50 | 0.3652 ms | 0.3515 ms | -3.8% |
| Host dispatch p95 | 0.5727 ms | 0.3884 ms | -32.2% |
| Host + device completion mean | 0.9498 ms | 0.8571 ms | -9.8% |

`msprof` showed that 11 synchronous D2H copies and 11 stream
synchronizations
were replaced by pinned asynchronous copies and 11 event
synchronizations. The
event was recorded before the first permutation was enqueued and waited
after
the permutation was already queued.

## A3 official end-to-end benchmark

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --temperature 0 --seed 42 --ignore-eos
```

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 16/16 | 16/16 | - |
| Mean TTFT | 1088.13 ms | 1081.25 ms | -0.63% |
| Median TTFT | 1090.04 ms | 1078.48 ms | -1.06% |
| P99 TTFT | 1097.65 ms | 1095.01 ms | -0.24% |
| Total throughput | 7526.18 tok/s | 7574.49 tok/s | +0.64% |

## A3 EvalScope accuracy

GSM8K was evaluated with 16 samples, greedy decoding, seed 42, and
`max_tokens=512`.

| Implementation | Accuracy | Correct |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 87.5% | 14/16 |
| Candidate | 87.5% | 14/16 |

All 16 per-sample accuracy decisions matched between baseline and
candidate.

## Implementation scope

The changes are limited to `TokenDispatcherWithAll2AllV` in
`vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py`, focused unit tests, and
a
release note.

[Test] Fix Triton being disabled in E2E-upstream and enable media cache (#22020)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
**1. Match the Dockerfile install order so Triton is not disabled**
E2E-upstream installed vllm-ascend and its dependencies in a single
`uv pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` transaction. That transaction
unpacks
both `triton==3.6.0` (pulled in by vllm) and
`triton-ascend==3.6.0.post2` into
the same `site-packages/triton`, and uv does not guarantee which one
lands last.
When the stock wheel won, `from triton.backends import backends` tried
to load
the Ascend entry point, `from triton._C.libtriton.ascend import ir`
raised
ImportError, and vLLM fell back to `TritonPlaceholder`. Every Triton
kernel then
became a plain function, so `kernel[(grid,)]` failed with
`TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable` during EngineCore
startup
(`_dummy_sampler_run` → `gumbel_sample`). The `patch_triton` patches
were also
skipped, because they are only imported when `HAS_TRITON` is true.
The Dockerfile avoids this by installing vllm-ascend with pip: pip
resolves and
installs `triton==3.6.0` first, then unpacks `triton-ascend` over it.
This PR
makes the workflow do the same — `pip install -e .` before
`uv pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` — so the two wheels are no
longer
unpacked in one transaction.
**2. Enable the media download cache**
The offline jobs now set `VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE` and a long
`VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE_TTL_HOURS`. `/root/.cache` is bind-mounted from the
runner
host, so media fetched once is reused across runs instead of hitting S3
on every
attempt, which previously caused flaky failures with
`503 Service Unavailable` while downloading test assets.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No, CI only.
### How was this patch tested?
CI-testing

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

[Feature][Kimi] Compose PCP prefill and DCP with DSpark (#22181)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Compose Kimi SFA PCP prefill with DCP-sharded caches on the current main
implementation, and allow Kimi MLA DSpark to use the same physical DCP
group. For a target such as TP1/PP4/PCP8/DCP8, the upstream draft
constructor currently revalidates the replicated PCP=1 query view as a
new worker topology and rejects it.

- During PCP prefill, gather only the referenced main/indexer KV pages
and compute attention and top-k for local query rows. Keep persistent
writes sharded, include ranks without local queries in the collectives,
and preserve the existing decode-only path.
- Remap compact history addresses using the KV interleave and actual
collective rank order. Preserve main's valid-block counts so stale
block-table tails are excluded from gathers, and keep unused table
addresses in bounds without changing valid KV addresses.
- Use the model's configured `index_topk` when selecting from gathered
indexer history. This keeps the selected indices and shared IndexCache
buffer at the same width, including at 1024.
- Kimi MLA DSpark takes its physical PCP/DCP group and KV interleave
from the target. The worker scopes the adaptation to the common DSpark
constructor and model loader, so it covers both the upstream runner's
temporary draft and the Ascend draft. The loader validates the physical
topology and exposes PCP=1 for replicated draft queries. The speculative
draft descriptor uses the upstream defaults.
- Copy the prepared draft's device sequence lengths to the CPU with
blocking `copy_`, including DCP>1. This uses rejection-corrected lengths
rather than the target CPU upper bound plus draft width. Remove
premature and duplicate copies so regular metadata and graph updates use
one current length snapshot.

#### Target and DSpark rank layout

One TP1 prefill stage uses the same eight ranks for PCP8 and DCP8. In
this example, rank 7 has no target query rows but still contributes its
KV pages to both history gathers.

#### Kimi K3.1 Pro with MegaMoE on eight A5 hosts

With the full 896-expert W4A8 MXFP model, DSpark and MegaMoE enabled on
prefill, **DCP8 served 131,072-token prompts in both prefix-cache
modes**. DCP1 failed the startup KV capacity check in both modes. The
run used PR revision `3e1562c30ba9`, the packed-FP4 weight view from
[#22333](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22333) at
`5dab7fda9746`, and a test-only fix that restored the target's MegaMoE
configuration after draft construction. All 32 prefill workers logged
CANN MegaMoE calls at DCP8.

The prefill engine used PP4/PCP8/TP1, `enable_fused_mc2=2`, memory
utilization 0.90, and a maximum sequence length of 140,000. The decode
topology and formal request payloads were fixed. Each completed workload
used concurrency 12, 20 requests and one output token. TTFT is measured
at the prefill server. QPS is end to end. Both are means of three formal
rounds.

| Prefill prefix cache | DCP1 startup KV required / available | DCP8
logical KV capacity | DCP8 mean TTFT | DCP8 QPS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| On, 90% shared input prefix | 0.72 / 0.35 GiB | 528,888 tokens |
12.061 s | 0.7600 |
| Off, same inputs | 0.70 / 0.36 GiB | 595,000 tokens | 42.721 s |
0.2023 |

**Warm-up and TTFT.** Two separate 120-request runs of the same earlier
PR revision (`9934127d`) had mean client TTFTs of **9.015 s and 6.715
s**. Each primed the shared prefix with one request at concurrency 1,
but neither warmed up at the measured concurrency of 12. The first 24
requests averaged **19.01 s and 7.31 s**. The remaining 96 averaged
**6.52 s and 6.57 s**. The gap was concentrated at startup, consistent
with insufficient warm-up at load. The seeds and payload hashes also
differed, so these runs cannot isolate the effect of warm-up or a code
change.

**Where a follow-up could improve performance.** A separate DCP8 +
MegaMoE run (`18c725191a36` +
[#22333](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22333) at
`a45c664d76c3`, concurrency 12, 120 requests, 90% shared prefix,
profiler off) reached **0.4415 QPS** and **25.921 s mean client TTFT**.
The tightest prefill rank had **0.25 GiB** available for KV. In 22 of 27
scheduler samples, one request was running and ten were waiting. For
this topology, keeping DSpark's 16,384-token budget and separately
sizing the target MegaMoE buffer for 14,776 rows per rank reduces the
CANN 9.3 **planner estimate** from **11.323 to 10.231 GiB per rank**. If
the released memory reaches the KV pool, prefill should be able to admit
more requests and reduce queueing. The proposed change and its effect on
TTFT and QPS still need an on-device comparison with identical inputs
and a concurrency-12 warm-up.

+    # the receiver's query rows are deliberately not in global request order.

+    gathered_key = torch.cat(

+    ).view(keys.dtype)
+    gathered_scale = torch.cat([scales[order.index(rank)].index_select(0, ids) for rank in range(world)])

+            dense[mask] = local_key * local_scale
+        restored_key = _index_select_kv_blocks(gathered_key, table[row]).float().reshape(-1, width)

+            selected = scores.topk(16).indices
+            selections.append(selected)
+            outputs.append(scores[selected].softmax(-1) @ history[selected])

[Test] fix weekly case (#22381)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix weekly test configurations where the requested output length exceeds
the serving context limit or leaves insufficient room for input tokens.

- Increase context limits for DeepSeek-V4-Flash Memcache PD accuracy,
Qwen3.8 PP2-TP2, Qwen3.5-397B PD, and Qwen3.6 accuracy cases.
- Reduce the AIME2025 output limit for the Qwen3.5-122B weekly case to
65536.
- Run Kimi-K3.1 GPQA after the performance benchmarks and reduce its
output limit to 65536.
- Remove the legacy model-runner override and explicit static-kernel
enablement from the GLM-5.2 layerwise PD case.
- Remove the DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefix-cache PD weekly configuration and
its dispatch entry.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This PR only updates SIT and weekly CI configurations.

[DevContainer][Feature] Add Dev Container environment settings for 310P/A2/A3/A5/CPU (#21789)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds Dev Container configurations under `.devcontainer/` so contributors
can get a
reproducible vLLM Ascend development environment with a single click in
VS Code /
Dev Containers, without manual CANN, torch_npu and build-toolchain
setup.

### Added environments

| Directory | Target hardware | Base image | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.devcontainer/310p` | Atlas 300I (310P) |
`quay.io/ascend/cann:9.1.0-310p-ubuntu22.04-py3.12` |
`SOC_VERSION=ascend310p1` |
| `.devcontainer/a2` | Ascend 910B (A2) |
`quay.io/ascend/cann:9.1.0-910b-ubuntu22.04-py3.12` | includes ATB env +
`triton-ascend==3.2.2`, clang-15 |
| `.devcontainer/a3` | Ascend 910C (A3) |
`quay.io/ascend/cann:9.1.0-a3-ubuntu22.04-py3.12` | same as A2 with
`SOC_VERSION=ascend910_9391` |
| `.devcontainer/a5` | Ascend 950 (A5) |
`quay.io/ascend/cann:9.1.0-950-ubuntu22.04-py3.12` |
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`/`MAX_JOBS=16` for faster builds |
| `.devcontainer/cpu` | CPU-only lint & UT |
`ascendai/python:3.12-ubuntu22.04` | no custom kernels, mocks
`vllm.cumem_allocator` for UT |

### Common features

- Binds the repo at `/workspace/vllm-ascend` and forwards ports
`8000`/`8080` for
  local OpenAI-compatible server testing.
- `postCreateCommand` installs system deps, sources the CANN/ATB
environment,
installs `requirements-dev.txt` plus the project in editable mode (`pip
install -e .`),
  and installs `coverage`.
- Named volumes cache pip and ccache (`vllm-ascend-<hw>-pip-cache` /
`-ccache`) to
  make container rebuilds fast.
- Pre-configures Ruff format/lint on save and common extensions (Python,
Pylance,
Ruff, GitLens, EditorConfig, YAML/TOML), so editor behavior matches
`format.sh ci`.
- Mounts the host `.ssh` (read-only) and copies the host `.gitconfig` on
start, so
  commits can be signed off with the contributor's existing identity.

### Why needed

Onboarding and reproducing NPU issues currently requires a long,
error-prone manual
setup and drifts across CANN / triton-ascend versions. These configs pin
the toolchain
per hardware target, reduce "works on my machine" issues, and make it
easier for
reviewers to reproduce bug reports.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, but developer-facing only: it adds a new optional way to set up a
development
environment (Dev Containers). No runtime, API, model or behavior changes
to vLLM
Ascend itself. This is tooling / CI-adjacent, so no
`release_notes/fragments` entry
is added.

## How was this patch tested?

Manual testing on VS Code + Dev Containers:

1. Open the repository root and run `Dev Containers: Reopen in
Container`, selecting
   each of the 310P / A2 / A3 / A5 / CPU configurations.
2. Verified the container builds, `postCreateCommand` completes, and
`source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh` is available in new
shells.
3. Verified `pip show vllm-ascend`, `python -c "import vllm_ascend"` and
   `npu-smi info` (on NPU targets) succeed.
4. Verified `bash format.sh ci` runs in the CPU container and that
`tests/ut`
   collects / executes with the `vllm.cumem_allocator` mock.

No unit tests are added because the change only contains Dev Container
JSON
configuration; behavior is validated manually by container startup and
the commands
above.

+# Hy4 (Experimental)
+
+## 1 Introduction
+
+!!! note
+
+    PD separation is provided as a reference deployment. For customer production deployments, follow the [MindIE Motor](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/en/mindie/latest/quickstart/docs/en/user_guide/quick_start.md) + vLLM Ascend deployment guidance.
+
+This release has been validated only on 950DT products. A2 and A3 have not yet been validated; support is planned for future releases.
+
+This guide describes Hy4 FP8 deployment with vLLM Ascend on 950DT products. It covers single-node co-located serving, two-node co-located serving, and four-node Prefill/Decode (PD) separation. Each host uses eight NPUs.
+
+The serving examples use compressed-tensors FP8 weights, expert parallelism, prefix caching, and MTP speculative decoding. The four-node PD configuration has been run successfully on 950DT products and used for measurement. It remains an experimental reference deployment.
+
+Hy4 uses the DFly2 architecture for its speculative module, not native MTP. It reuses vLLM's MTP method name for configuration: set `"method": "mtp"` in the speculative config to enable DFly2 speculative decoding.
+
+## 2 Supported Features
+
+Refer to the [Supported Models](../../user_guide/support_matrix/supported_models.md) page for the support matrix and the [Feature Guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/index.md) for feature configuration.
+
+## 3 Prerequisites
+
+### 3.1 Model Weight
+
+Use the `tencent/Hy4-FP8` checkpoint from [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-FP8) or [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy4-FP8). Download the complete checkpoint, including its tokenizer, model configuration, multimodal processor files, and weights required by MTP. Make it accessible at `/path/to/Hy4-FP8` inside every serving container. Use the same checkpoint revision on every host.
+
+### 3.2 Verify Multi-node Communication
+
+For multi-node deployment, follow [multi-node interconnect preparation](../../getting_started/installation.md#installation-multi-node-interconnect). Choose mutually reachable host IPs and the corresponding local network interfaces. Ensure HCCL connectivity and access to the API, DP coordinator, and KV transfer ports.
+
+## 4 Installation
+
+### 4.1 Docker Image Installation
+
+Use the Hy4 openEuler image `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:hy4-1120-a5-openeuler` on 950DT products. The deployment was validated with the following software versions:
+
+| Hardware | Ascend HDK | CANN version | torch_npu version | vLLM | vLLM-Ascend version |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 950DT products | 25.1.rc3 | CANN 9.1.0 | 2.10.0.post4 | v0.30.0 | Based on v0.30.0 |
+
+Use matching vLLM, vLLM Ascend, CANN, and torch-npu versions on every host.
+
+Follow [Installation](../../getting_started/installation.md) for the container setup appropriate to the hardware. On every host:
+
+- Expose NPU devices 0–7 and the required management devices.
+- Mount the Ascend driver, firmware, and communication configuration required by the hardware.
+- Use host networking and sufficient shared memory.
+- Mount the weights at /path/to/Hy4-FP8.
+- Make the matching repositories accessible at /path/to/vllm-ascend and /path/to/vllm. PD scripts use both through PYTHONPATH.
+
+The following container template uses the Hy4 openEuler image for 950DT products. Use the matching device and communication mounts for your environment. The host model and repository directories must already contain the complete checkpoint and matching code.
+
+```bash
+export IMAGE="quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:hy4-1120-a5-openeuler"
+export CONTAINER_NAME=hy4
+export MODEL_DIR="/path/to/Hy4-FP8"
+export WORK_DIR="/path/to/hy4-workspace"
+mkdir -p "$WORK_DIR"
+
+docker run \
+    -it \
+    --name "$CONTAINER_NAME" \
+    --network host \
+    --ipc host \
+    --privileged \
+    --shm-size=100g \
+    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
+    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
+    --device /dev/ummu \
+    --device /dev/uburma \
+    --device /dev/davinci0 \
+    --device /dev/davinci1 \
+    --device /dev/davinci2 \
+    --device /dev/davinci3 \
+    --device /dev/davinci4 \
+    --device /dev/davinci5 \
+    --device /dev/davinci6 \
+    --device /dev/davinci7 \

+## 5 Online Service Deployment
+
+### 5.1 Single-Node Co-located Deployment
+
+=== "950DT products"
+
+    Run on the single serving host. Provide sufficient host RAM for prefetch weight offloading; the RAM requirement remains to be measured.
+
+    ```bash
+    set -euo pipefail
+
+    set +u
+    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
+    set -u
+    cd /path/to/vllm-ascend
+
+    MODEL=/path/to/Hy4-FP8
+    PORT=8000
+
+    export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
+    export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=128
+    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
+    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
+    export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=10800
+
+    exec vllm serve "${MODEL}" \
+        --host 0.0.0.0 \
+        --port "${PORT}" \
+        --data-parallel-size 1 \
+        --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+        --served-model-name Hy4 \

+### 5.2 Two-Node Co-located Deployment
+
+=== "950DT products"
+
+    Save the following as start_colocated.sh on both hosts. Set NODE0_IP to the same coordinator address on both hosts. Set NODE_IP and NIC for the local host. Select the indicated FRONTEND_ARGS for each node: node 0 exposes port 8000 and node 1 is headless.
+
+    Start node 0 first. Once its DP coordinator has started, start node 1 in another terminal. Both processes must remain running; increasing the readiness timeout does not replace starting the peer.
+
+    ```bash
+    #!/usr/bin/env bash
+    set -euo pipefail
+
+    set +u
+    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
+    set -u
+    cd /path/to/vllm-ascend
+
+    NODE0_IP="<NODE0_IP>"
+    NODE_IP="<LOCAL_IP>"
+    NIC="<NIC_NAME>"
+    MODEL=/path/to/Hy4-FP8
+
+    # DP2 x TP8 across two hosts, one DP replica per host, EP16.
+    export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
+    export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
+    export VLLM_HOST_IP=${NODE_IP}
+    export HCCL_IF_IP=${NODE_IP}
+    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=${NIC}
+    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=${NIC}
+    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
+    unset HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE
+    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
+    # Frontend readiness includes the remote engine; this does not fix a missing peer.
+    export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=10800
+
+    # Node 0:
+    FRONTEND_ARGS=(--api-server-count 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000)
+    # Node 1: replace the line above with:
+    # FRONTEND_ARGS=(--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 1)
+
+    exec vllm serve "${MODEL}" \
+        "${FRONTEND_ARGS[@]}" \
+        --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+        --data-parallel-size 2 \
+        --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
+        --data-parallel-backend mp \
+        --data-parallel-address "${NODE0_IP}" \
+        --data-parallel-rpc-port 12890 \
+        --enable-expert-parallel \
+        --served-model-name Hy4 \
+        --distributed-executor-backend mp \
+        --quantization compressed-tensors \
+        --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
+        --max-num-seqs 256 \
+        --max-model-len 163840 \
+        --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
+        --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
+        --enable-prefix-caching \
+        --enable-chunked-prefill \
+        --no-async-scheduling \
+        --seed 0 \
+        --compilation-config '{
+          "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"
+        }' \
+        --speculative-config '{
+          "method": "mtp",
+          "num_speculative_tokens": 5,
+          "draft_load_config": {},
+          "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"
+        }' \
+        --additional-config '{
+          "weight_nz_mode": 1,
+          "sparse_kv_offload_config": {
+            "enabled": false
+          },
+          "enable_mlapo": true,
+          "enable_fused_mc2": 1,
+          "ascend_compilation_config": {
+            "enable_npugraph_ex": false
+          }
+        }'
+    ```

+### 5.3 Four-Node PD Separation
+
+=== "950DT products"
+
+    Use four distinct hosts. P0/P1 form one DP2 × TP8 group, and D0/D1 form another. Only P0 and D0 expose HTTP APIs. The proxy routes requests to those group frontends.
+
+    | Host | DP rank | API port | DP coordinator | KV role | KV rank | KV port |
+    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+    | P0 | 0 | 18010 | P0:12890 | kv_producer | 0 | 23000 |
+    | P1 | 1, headless | — | P0:12890 | kv_producer | 0 | 23000 |
+    | D0 | 0 | 18020 | D0:12891 | kv_consumer | 1 | 24000 |
+    | D1 | 1, headless | — | D0:12891 | kv_consumer | 1 | 24000 |
+
+    The KV ranks follow the supplied scripts and identify P/D groups separately from DP ranks. The reference deployment uses five MTP speculative tokens and HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024 on all four hosts.
+
+    Save the following files in the same directory on every host.
+
+    **config.sh**
+
+    ```bash
+    #!/usr/bin/env bash
+    ASCEND_REPO=/path/to/vllm-ascend
+    VLLM_REPO=/path/to/vllm
+    MODEL=/path/to/Hy4-FP8
+    QUANTIZATION=compressed-tensors
+    NIC="<NIC_NAME>"
+    ```
+
+    Set NIC separately on each host if interface names differ.
+
+    **start_common.sh**
+
+    ```bash
+    #!/usr/bin/env bash
+    # Run the corresponding role script inside each serving container.
+    set -eo pipefail
+    SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+    source "$SCRIPT_DIR/config.sh"
+    if [[ ${1:-} != --dry-run ]]; then source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh; fi
+    set -u
+    export PYTHONPATH="${ASCEND_REPO}:${VLLM_REPO}:${PYTHONPATH:-}"
+    export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
+    export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
+    export VLLM_HOST_IP="$NODE_IP" HCCL_IF_IP="$NODE_IP"
+    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=${NIC} GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=${NIC} TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=${NIC}
+    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
+    unset HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE
+    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
+    export NO_PROXY='*' no_proxy='*' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
+    args=(python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL"
+        --host 0.0.0.0 --port "$API_PORT"
+        --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size-local 1
+        --data-parallel-address "$MASTER_IP" --data-parallel-rpc-port "$DP_PORT"
+        --tensor-parallel-size 8 --served-model-name Hy4 --enable-expert-parallel
+        --distributed-executor-backend mp --quantization "$QUANTIZATION"
+        --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 147456 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
+        --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling --seed 0
+        --compilation-config '{
+          "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"
+        }'
+        --speculative-config '{
+          "method": "mtp",
+          "num_speculative_tokens": 5,
+          "draft_load_config": {}
+        }'
+        --additional-config '{
+          "weight_nz_mode": 1,
+          "sparse_kv_offload_config": {
+            "enabled": false
+          },
+          "enable_mlapo": true,
+          "enable_fused_mc2": 1,
+          "ascend_compilation_config": {
+            "enable_npugraph_ex": false
+          }
+        }'
+        --kv-transfer-config "{\"kv_connector\":\"MooncakeConnectorV1\",\"kv_buffer_device\":\"npu\",\"kv_role\":\"$KV_ROLE\",\"kv_rank\":$KV_RANK,\"kv_port\":$KV_PORT,\"kv_connector_extra_config\":{\"prefill\":{\"dp_size\":2,\"tp_size\":8},\"decode\":{\"dp_size\":2,\"tp_size\":8}}}")
+    if [ "$RANK" = 1 ]; then args+=(--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 1); fi
+    printf '%q ' "${args[@]}"; printf '\n'
+    if [ "${1:-}" = --dry-run ]; then exit 0; fi
+    exec "${args[@]}" "$@"
+    ```
+
+    **Role scripts**
+
+    Create one script per host using the following template and the values in the table. NODE_IP is the local host address; MASTER_IP is P0 for P roles and D0 for D roles.
+
+    ```bash
+    #!/usr/bin/env bash
+    NODE_IP="<LOCAL_IP>" MASTER_IP="<GROUP_MASTER_IP>" RANK=0 API_PORT=18010 DP_PORT=12890
+    KV_ROLE=kv_producer KV_RANK=0 KV_PORT=23000
+    source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/start_common.sh"
+    ```
+
+    | Script | NODE_IP | MASTER_IP | RANK | API_PORT | DP_PORT | KV_ROLE | KV_RANK | KV_PORT |
+    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+    | start_p0.sh | P0 IP | P0 IP | 0 | 18010 | 12890 | kv_producer | 0 | 23000 |
+    | start_p1.sh | P1 IP | P0 IP | 1 | 18010 | 12890 | kv_producer | 0 | 23000 |
+    | start_d0.sh | D0 IP | D0 IP | 0 | 18020 | 12891 | kv_consumer | 1 | 24000 |
+    | start_d1.sh | D1 IP | D0 IP | 1 | 18020 | 12891 | kv_consumer | 1 | 24000 |
+
+    Start P0, wait for its DP coordinator, then start P1. Start D0, wait for its DP coordinator, then start D1. Check both frontend health endpoints before starting the proxy:
+
+    ```bash
+    curl --fail "http://<P0_IP>:18010/health"
+    curl --fail "http://<D0_IP>:18020/health"
+    ```
+
+    **Proxy**
+
+    Run on a host that can reach P0 and D0. The proxy script must be present in the matching vLLM Ascend checkout.
+
+    ```bash
+    source ./config.sh
+    export PYTHONPATH="${ASCEND_REPO}:${VLLM_REPO}:${PYTHONPATH:-}"
+    export NO_PROXY='*' no_proxy='*'
+    python3 "$ASCEND_REPO/examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py" \
+        --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
+        --prefiller-hosts "<P0_IP>" --prefiller-ports 18010 \
+        --decoder-hosts "<D0_IP>" --decoder-ports 18020
+    ```
+
+    After preparing the files, use bash start_p0.sh --dry-run (or the corresponding role script) to inspect commands without starting an engine. A dry run does not validate model loading, graph capture, communication, or KV transfer.

+## 6 Functional Verification
+
+### 6.1 Text
+
+For co-located deployment, use the API host. For PD deployment, use the proxy host.
+
+```bash
+SERVER_IP="<API_OR_PROXY_IP>"
+curl --fail "http://${SERVER_IP}:8000/v1/models"
+curl --fail "http://${SERVER_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{
+        "model": "Hy4",
+        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 2?"}],
+        "max_tokens": 64,
+        "temperature": 0
+    }'
+```
+
+Confirm that the response uses model Hy4 and contains a valid answer. For PD, also confirm from both groups' logs that Prefill and Decode execute and KV transfer completes. An HTTP response alone is insufficient evidence of successful PD operation.
+
+### 6.2 Single Image
+
+Use a local image and send it as a base64 data URL to the same chat completions endpoint. The image is read on the curl client; it does not need to be mounted in the serving container. The example uses a PNG image. Change `IMAGE_MIME` to `image/jpeg` for a JPEG image, and replace the question with one appropriate to the image. For a HallusionBench sample, use its image and the corresponding dataset question.
+
+The four-node PD deployment supports multimodal requests and has been tested with image inputs. Send the following request to the proxy host to verify the deployed service.
+
+```bash
+SERVER_IP="<API_OR_PROXY_IP>"
+IMAGE_PATH=/path/to/image.png
+IMAGE_MIME=image/png
+IMAGE_BASE64=$(base64 < "$IMAGE_PATH" | tr -d '\n')
+
+curl --fail --show-error --noproxy '*' --max-time 180 \
+    "http://${SERVER_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    --data-binary @- <<EOF
+{
+    "model": "Hy4",
+    "messages": [
+        {
+            "role": "user",
+            "content": [
+                {
+                    "type": "image_url",
+                    "image_url": {
+                        "url": "data:${IMAGE_MIME};base64,${IMAGE_BASE64}"
+                    }
+                },
+                {
+                    "type": "text",
+                    "text": "Describe the objects visible in this image."
+                }
+            ]
+        }
+    ],
+    "max_tokens": 512,
+    "temperature": 0,
+    "stream": false,
+    "chat_template_kwargs": {
+        "reasoning_effort": "no_think"
+    }
+}
+EOF
+```
+
+Check that `choices[0].message.content` answers the image question and is consistent with the image. Inspect `finish_reason` and `usage` for truncation and token consumption. This single-image request is a functional check; HallusionBench accuracy requires running the dataset with its matching evaluator.

+## 9 Performance Tuning
+
+### 9.1 Reference Configurations
+
+Use the configuration table in [Supported Features](#2-supported-features) as the starting point for each topology. Single-node serving uses weight offloading and a small KV cache to reduce device memory requirements. Two-node serving distributes experts across both hosts without weight offloading. The PD example uses separate two-host groups for Prefill and Decode.
+
+### 9.2 Tuning Guidelines
+
+- Tune concurrency and token budgets against the actual available memory. A configured maximum model length does not establish that every request at that length can run at the configured maximum concurrency.
+- Account for host RAM and transfer bandwidth when using single-node prefetch weight offloading.
+- Compare MTP acceptance and latency with the same workload before changing the speculative token count. Keep the topology-specific scheduling settings until changes have been validated.
+- Keep the Prefill and Decode topology declarations consistent in both groups' KV connector configuration.
+
+## 10 FAQ
+
+### 10.1 Multi-node Startup Waits for a Peer
+
+Confirm that every DP rank has started, that the group coordinator address is consistent, and that each local IP belongs to the selected network interface. Check inter-node connectivity and coordinator ports. Increasing the engine readiness timeout does not resolve a missing or unreachable peer.
+
+### 10.2 Single-Node Deployment Runs Out of Memory
+
+Check both device memory and host RAM. The example uses prefetch weight offloading and an explicit KV cache allocation. Confirm that the weight-offload configuration is active before increasing sequence length, concurrency, or KV cache allocation.
+
+### 10.3 PD Requests Do Not Complete
+
+Check P0 and D0 health independently, then verify the proxy's frontend addresses and ports. Check both groups' logs for KV connector initialization and transfer errors. Confirm matching Mooncake versions and the DP/TP topology in both connector configurations.
